lab.title: Your first five minutes
lab.scenario: Practice reading context before acting. You will repeat this exact check every time you land on a new system.

steps.text: Run the identity check and confirm the prompt matches reality.
steps.verify: The username and hostname should match the prompt; pwd should be your home directory.

steps.text: Inspect system uptime and load averages.
steps.verify: The load averages are three numbers: 1, 5, and 15 minutes.

steps.text: Print your home directory using both single and double quotes. Compare the output.
steps.verify: Double quotes expand $HOME, while single quotes print it literally; the two outputs should differ.

steps.text: Find out whether cd is a shell builtin or an external binary.
steps.verify: It should report that cd is a shell builtin.

steps.text: Inspect your last commands and re-run one using history expansion.
steps.verify: history should list recent commands with numbers, and the expansion should run one of them again.

quiz.q: What does a prompt ending in # tell you?
options: The shell is in a container
quiz.why: A # prompt conventionally indicates root. A $ prompt indicates a regular user.

quiz.q: Which command shows the current directory?
quiz.why: pwd stands for print working directory. cd changes it; ls lists its contents.

quiz.q: What is the safest way to run one command as root?
options: Add your user to every group
quiz.why: sudo grants privilege for one command and leaves an audit trail. A permanent root shell removes friction and safety at the same time.
